The high-efficiency RTU upgrade measure results in a 6% reduction in total site energy consumption—equivalent to 295 TBtu—across the U.S. commercial building stock modeled in ComStock, including buildings not applicable to the upgrade scenario (the measure is only applicable to buildings with existing RTUs). The majority of these savings are driven by a 29% reduction in fan electricity use (197 TBtu) and a 15% reduction in cooling electricity use (112 TBtu), partially offset by a 1.4% increase in heating natural gas use (-13 TBtu). As discussed in Section 5.1, this trend reflects the improved efficiency of variable-speed RTUs, which reduce electricity demand for fans and cooling. However, the reduced waste heat from more efficient fan operation leads to a slight increase in heating requirements, contributing to the observed rise in natural gas consumption. Table 6.
